reason: A native Codex turn/steer carries no settings, and the bridge interrupts and restarts the turn only for permission changes, so a model change sent with a steer is ignored until the next turn.
An env var changed with a steer is not applied to the steered work; in the live recording the command after the steer printed the old value.
A reasoning level changed with a steer is ignored until the next turn, as for the model.

Claude Code applies model, reasoning and permission changes on a steer live, but an env var change needs a new CLI process and the bridge does not restart for a steer; in the live recording the command after the steer printed the old value.
The Pi bridge applies settings by restarting pi with new flags, which it does before follow-up turns but not for a steer.
As for the model: a steer does not restart pi, so the steered work keeps the old env; in the live recording the command after the steer printed the old value.
As for the model: a steer does not restart pi with the new --thinking level.
After the pi process dies mid-turn the bridge drops the session, and the next turn/start fails with "No active Pi session"; reproduced live.
Same cause as next-turn-runs: no replacement pi process is started, so the conversation does not continue.
